questions.passage: The Apollo Moon landings (1969-1972) brought atmospheric sensors and seismic sensors to the Moon and produced large amounts of data. Researcher Renee Weber, who is investigating tectonic activity on the Moon, continues to use Apollo's data, demonstrating that the missions' value to science is [vocab]______[/vocab].
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: displaced

choices.label: B
choices.text: ongoing

choices.label: C
choices.text: original

choices.label: D
choices.text: controversial

explanation.short: Ongoing means continuing: the Apollo data still have scientific value decades after collection.
explanation.key_evidence: The sensors collected data in 1969–1972, and Weber continues to use those data.
explanation.why_correct: B describes the persistence of the data's value from the Apollo era into later research. Their continuing use is direct evidence that their value is ongoing.
explanation.detailed: The contrast is temporal, not a dispute about quality. Although the original measurements are old, researchers can still learn from them. The blank therefore needs a word meaning continuing into the present. It does not need a word meaning replaced, novel, or disputed.

choice_analysis.A: Displaced means pushed aside or replaced; continued use gives no evidence that the scientific value has been displaced.
choice_analysis.B: Ongoing means continuing, matching the continuing scientific use of the old measurements.
choice_analysis.C: Original can mean initial or novel, but the example establishes lasting value rather than originality.
choice_analysis.D: Controversial means disputed, and the passage describes no disagreement about the data's scientific value.

questions.passage: Because cyanobacteria and other microphytobenthos (MPB)—microscopic organisms inhabiting tidal flats—are consumed by mussels as well as by certain shorebirds and fish, MPB are [vocab]______[/vocab] estuary ecosystems. Decreased MPB abundance, which may be caused by environmental stressors, thus has a direct, negative impact on coastal food webs.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: imperative for

choices.label: B
choices.text: emblematic of

choices.label: C
choices.text: subordinate to

choices.label: D
choices.text: interchangeable with

explanation.short: Imperative for means essential to, matching MPB's important role in the estuary food web.
explanation.key_evidence: MPB provide food for mussels and other organisms, and a decline in MPB would harm the wider food web.
explanation.why_correct: A connects MPB's role as a food source to the health of estuary ecosystems. The predicted harm from their decline supports their importance to those ecosystems.
explanation.detailed: Follow the ecological chain: MPB feed organisms that participate in a broader food web. Reducing MPB would therefore affect more than the microbes themselves. The blank summarizes their crucial supporting role. No evidence makes MPB an emblem of estuaries, ranks them below estuaries, or treats them as exchangeable with whole ecosystems.

choice_analysis.A: Imperative for means essential or crucial to and fits the stated consequences of an MPB decline.
choice_analysis.B: Emblematic of means representative or symbolic of; the passage concerns ecological function, not symbolism.
choice_analysis.C: Subordinate to means lower in rank or importance than; no such hierarchy is established, and this misses their crucial food-web role.
choice_analysis.D: Interchangeable with means able to replace one another. MPB and entire ecosystems are not presented as substitutes.

questions.passage: Some pieces of music might have many meanings—the compositions of Charlotte Moorman can [vocab]______[/vocab] as many different interpretations as there are people to listen to them—and so as long as a listener's interpretation isn't willfully absurd or the result of inattention, it is difficult to justify the claim that the listener has misunderstood the piece.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: refute

choices.label: B
choices.text: omit

choices.label: C
choices.text: support

choices.label: D
choices.text: evade

explanation.short: Support means sustain or allow: the compositions can sustain many reasonable interpretations.
explanation.key_evidence: It is difficult to justify saying a listener misunderstood unless the interpretation is absurd or inattentive.
explanation.why_correct: C explains why reasonable listeners need not arrive at one identical meaning. The compositions can support multiple interpretations without every alternative being a misunderstanding.
explanation.detailed: The surrounding statements emphasize music's openness to different meanings. The exception for absurd or inattentive readings still leaves many defensible readings. Thus the blank needs a verb expressing the compositions' capacity to sustain those readings, not to reject, leave out, or avoid them.

choice_analysis.A: Refute means disprove; disproving many interpretations would conflict with the passage's emphasis on interpretive openness.
choice_analysis.B: Omit means leave out. Although it can grammatically take interpretations as an object, exclusion is not the meaning required here.
choice_analysis.C: Support means sustain or provide a basis for, fitting the many reasonable interpretations the compositions permit.
choice_analysis.D: Evade means avoid or escape; the text says the music accommodates interpretations, not that it avoids them.

questions.passage: The inventories of consonant sounds among the Polynesian languages of the Pacific tend toward the [vocab]______[/vocab]: Sikaiana in the South Pacific has a total of nine consonants, and ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, the language of the Native Hawaiian people, has one fewer, while the global median per language is over twenty-two.

choices.text: static

choices.label: D

explanation.short: Minimal precisely describes consonant inventories much smaller than the global median.
explanation.key_evidence: The cited languages have only eight or nine consonants, far below the global median of over twenty-two.
explanation.why_correct: The local context fixes the needed meaning: Minimal precisely describes consonant inventories much smaller than the global median. That meaning is expressed precisely by “minimal”.
explanation.detailed: The decisive evidence is that the named languages have nine and eight consonants, far below the global median of over twenty-two. Minimal precisely describes consonant inventories much smaller than the global median.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“minimal”) is correct. Minimal means very small, matching the comparison.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“static”) is incorrect. Static concerns change over time.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“replicable”) is incorrect. Replicable concerns being reproduced.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“melodic”) is incorrect. Melodic concerns musical quality, not inventory size.

explanation.detailed: The decisive evidence is that a tempest rages over the ocean while Puerto Cabello's land-locked waters move easily and gently. The imagery contrasts the violent open ocean with the gentle waters near Puerto Cabello.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“It describes the speaker's attitude towards the day-to-day life in Puerto Cabello.”) is incorrect. The focus is not everyday life.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“It contrasts the tranquility of the waters near Puerto Cabello with the roughness of waters elsewhere.”) is correct. This directly states the poem's central contrast.

explanation.detailed: The decisive evidence is that the text says non-Indigenous museums anticipate mainly non-Indigenous audiences. Unlike the Indigenous-led centers, the museums are described as designing displays chiefly for non-Indigenous audiences.

Due to Hawaii's uniquely varied geographic and ecological conditions, the kiwikiu became highly specialized as it adapted to survive in a specific island habitat. questions.passage: The following text is adapted from Guy de Maupassant's 1884 short story "A Recollection," from the collection [i]Guy de Maupassant Short Stories[/i] (translated by Albert M.C. McMaster et al. in 1903). The narrator is taking a boat down the Seine river from Paris, France, to the surrounding countryside. questions.passage: Paleontologist Amane Tajika and colleagues analyzed the shells of two marine mollusks called nautilids that were collected from waters near New Caledonia. choices.label: A
choices.text: New Caledonia nautilids tend to migrate upward to warmer water immediately after hatching, whereas Fijian nautilids do not.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The water temperature at a given depth tends to be higher in waters near Fiji than it is at that depth in waters near New Caledonia.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

explanation.short: If Fiji is warmer than New Caledonia at the same depth, greater Fijian nesting depth does not establish that Fiji eggs are in colder water.
explanation.key_evidence: A shallower egg depth does not establish warmer water if water at the same depth near Fiji is warmer than near New Caledonia.
explanation.why_correct: The passage asks for evidence that directly bears on the stated claim: If Fiji is warmer than New Caledonia at the same depth, greater Fijian nesting depth does not establish that Fiji eggs are in colder water. That evidentiary link is supplied by choice B.
explanation.detailed: The decisive evidence is that the hypothesis treats shallower New Caledonian egg depth as warmer; temperatures could instead differ between regions at the same depth. If Fiji is warmer than New Caledonia at the same depth, greater Fijian nesting depth does not establish that Fiji eggs are in colder water.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“New Caledonia nautilids tend to migrate upward to warmer water immediately after hatching, whereas Fijian nautilids do not.”) is incorrect. Post-hatching migration does not compare egg-laying temperatures.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“The water temperature at a given depth tends to be higher in waters near Fiji than it is at that depth in waters near New Caledonia.”) is correct. Regional temperature differences directly weaken the depth-based inference.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“There aren't enough suitable hatching areas at a depth of at least 170 meters in New Caledonia for nautilids to lay their eggs at that depth.”) is incorrect. Suitable nesting sites do not establish temperatures.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“The water temperature at a given depth tends to be lower in waters near Fiji than it is at that depth in waters near New Caledonia.”) is incorrect. This would make Fiji's deeper water even colder and support the hypothesis.

Choice B most directly weakens the proxy proposal: if the two species take up WC-NPs differently in an unknown way, results from water lice may not substitute for frog sampling. The other choices do not show that the proxy would be unreliable.
